title: Transitrix ingest review queue
description: The human gate produced by the ingest pipeline for one batch. It lists the field artefacts (with proposed source_quality), the canon candidates (with derived_from, extraction_confidence, and any validation / coverage flags), and the below-threshold relation suggestions. NOTHING in this queue is admitted to canon — a human reviews, confirms or revises each proposed source_quality, and runs the canon admission gate to admit candidates.

generated_by.description: Tool identifier that produced the queue (e.g. the ingest CLI version).

org_root.description: Path to the adopter organisation root this batch was ingested into.

sources.description: The raw source files this batch derived from, retained under _intake/processed/.

coverage_profile.description: The adopter's active coverage_profile that candidates were checked against (COVERAGE_PROFILES.md).

field_artefacts.description: Source artefacts the candidates in this batch derive from. A FIELD artefact (interview/survey/observation/draft) carries a PROPOSED source_quality for the human to confirm; a CODEX artefact (law/regulation/policy/standard) is authoritative by construction and carries no source_quality (zone: codex, authoritative: true).

zone.description: Which zone the artefact was resolved from. Omitted on a field artefact for backward compatibility.

found.description: Whether the cited artefact resolved to a file on disk.

proposed_source_quality.description: Field-zone only — the proposed trust level for the human to confirm. Absent on a codex artefact (authoritative by construction).

authoritative.description: Codex-zone only — true; a codex source needs no source_quality confirmation.

effective_date.description: Codex-zone only — the source's effective date.

source_hash.description: Content fingerprint of the raw bytes, surfaced for the reviewer (e.g. to compare against an inbox copy).

duplicate_sources.description: Optional. Clusters of source artefacts that share a source_hash — the same content admitted more than once (e.g. via admit-source --force). Present only when at least one cluster exists; the human collapses duplicates before admitting candidates derived from both.

entity_match_proposals.description: Optional. Candidates whose name matched an existing canon element's name or alias (F8 cross-source entity resolution). Surfaced for the human gate: decide whether each candidate is a duplicate of the existing element (reference its id) or genuinely new (admit with a fresh id). Propose, never auto-merge. Present only when at least one match exists.

matched_on.description: Whether the match was on the existing element's primary name or one of its aliases.

proposed_existing_id.description: Canonical ID of the existing element this candidate may be referring to.

candidates.description: Canon candidates awaiting the human admission gate. Each conforms to candidate.schema.json; the queue references them and surfaces their flags.

ref.description: Path or ID of the candidate file.

relation_suggestions.description: Relations that fell below the conservative emission threshold (Step 4). Surfaced as SUGGESTIONS for the reviewer, never emitted as candidates.

reason.description: Why it was held back (e.g. below confidence threshold, ambiguous endpoint).

semantic_links.description: Optional. Review-only typed edges between candidates (or between a candidate and an admitted element) for which no closed REL kind exists (17-relations.md §3) — distinct from relation_suggestions, which holds back a real rel_kind on low confidence. A semantic link is never shaped into a relation candidate and never admitted to canon; once a canonical relation kind covers the edge, re-extract it as a relation candidate instead. Present only when at least one link exists.

link_type.description: Free-form label for the suspected edge (e.g. 'requirement_dependency'). Not a closed REL kind — never validated against 17-relations.md, never written to a rel_kind field.

from.description: Source endpoint — a candidate ref or canonical element ID.

to.description: Target endpoint — a candidate ref or canonical element ID.

rationale.description: Why the extractor suspects this edge — the reviewer's basis for confirming or discarding it.

gate.description: Invariant statement for auditors and tooling: this skill admits nothing.
